previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with primary sclerosing cholangitis and Child-Pugh class B cirrhosis, on the transplant list, was admitted with a 10-day history of malaise, weakness, and right upper quadrant abdominal pain consistent with recurrent cholangitis. She had no fevers but reported low-grade temperatures and arthralgias. Labs showed transaminitis with stable bilirubin and normal renal function. Blood and urine cultures were negative. Imaging revealed coarsened liver architecture, splenomegaly, and a gallbladder remnant with stones, but no biliary dilation or ascites. She was treated with IV antibiotics, transitioned to ertapenem, and received a PICC line for outpatient administration. Her oral vancomycin for prior C. difficile infection was continued. Her symptoms improved, liver enzymes trended downward, and MELD score improved from 10 to 8. She was discharged home with home nursing for daily IV antibiotics until transplant and instructions to continue oral vancomycin for two weeks after IV therapy completion.

PROCEDURE:
1. Intraoperative direct access to a first order superior mesenteric vein
branch.
2. Superior mesenteric venogram.
3. Recanalization of a narrowed main portal vein followed by intrahepatic
portal venography.
4. Successive catheterization, venography and coil embolization of 4
esophageal varices.
5. Splenic venogram.
6. Inferior mesenteric venogram.
7. Catheterization, venography and embolization of the inferior mesenteric
vein using a 12 mm Amplatz her plug and 0.035 questionable coils.
8. Post embolization Splenic venography.
9. Recanalization of a nearly occluded main portal vein.
10. Intrahepatic portal venography.
11. Balloon angioplasty of the main portal vein with an 8 mm balloon.
12. Covered stenting of the main portal vein with a 10 mm x 2.5 cm via Bond

PROCEDURE:
1. Right internal jugular venous access using ultrasound.
2. Pre balloon angioplasty right atrial and right hepatic vein pressure
measurements

4. Right hepatic vein/inferior vena cava anastomotic balloon angioplasty with
10 mm balloon.

pressure measurements

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The right neck was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Under continuous ultrasound guidance, the patent right internal jugular vein
was compressible and accessed using a micropuncture needle. Hard copy
ultrasound images were obtained before and after intravenous access.
Subsequently a Nitinol wire was passed into the right atrium using
fluoroscopic guidance. A small incision was made at the needle entry site. The
needle was exchanged for a micropuncture sheath. The Nitinol wire was removed
and a short ___ wire was advanced distally into the IVC.

A 10 ___ sheath was advanced over the wire into the inferior vena cava over
the wire.  The inner dilator was removed.  Using a SOS catheter and a
Glidewire, access was obtained in the right hepatic vein. Appropriate position
was confirmed with contrast injection and lateral fluoroscopy. The Glidewire
was exchanged for ___ wire and the sheath was advanced into the proximal
right hepatic vein. Then, the SOS catheter was exchanged for a straight flush
catheter.  The sheath was retracted into the right atrium.  A contrast right
hepatic venogram was performed.  Pressure measurements of the right hepatic
vein via the straight flush catheter and right atrium via the sheath were
obtained.  The straight flush catheter was exchanged for a 10 mm Mustang
balloon.  Serial balloon dilatations of the right hepatic vein/inferior vena
cava anastomosis were performed.  The balloon catheter was exchanged for the
straight flush catheter which was advanced into the right hepatic vein. The
wire was removed. A small hand contrast injection confirmed placement within
the right hepatic vein. A post balloon angioplasty right hepatic venogram was
then performed.

The sheath was advanced over the catheter into the right hepatic vein. The
catheter and ___ wire were removed.  A liver access sheath was advanced into
the liver in appropriate position. The biopsy needle was advanced through the
liver access sheath and three 18 gauge core biopsies were acquired while
pointing the biopsy sheath anteriorly. The core biopsies were placed in
formalin and labeled for pathology.

The liver access sheath and biopsy needle were discarded.  The straight flush
catheter was advanced directly into the sheath into the right hepatic vein. 
The sheath and straight flush catheter were retracted into the inferior vena
cava.  Post balloon angioplasty right hepatic vein, inferior vena cava and
right atrial pressure measurements were obtained.  The proximal inferior vena
cavagram was performed.

The catheter and sheath were removed.  Manual pressure was held until
hemostasis was achieved and sterile dressings were applied. The patient
tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate post-procedure
complications.

FINDINGS:


1. Small nonocclusive thrombus in the right internal jugular vein
2. Contrast-enhanced right hepatic venogram demonstrated stenosis of the right
hepatic vein/inferior vena cava anastomosis
3. Right hepatic vein - right atrial gradient of 25 mm per Hg
4. Successful balloon angioplasty of the right hepatic vein/inferior vena cava
anastomosis with moderate luminal gain with a 10 mm balloon.
5. Post balloon angioplasty right hepatic vein - right atrial gradient of 17
mm per Hg
6. Successful transjugular approach core biopsy with 3 passes
7. Right atrial - inferior vena cava gradient of 5 mm per Hg

Successful transjugular low core biopsy. Successful balloon angioplasty of the
right hepatic vein - inferior vena cava anastomosis with reduction of gradient
from 25 mm per Hg to 17 mm per Hg.  Small nonocclusive thrombus within the
right internal jugular vein.

obstruction by biopsy, repeat balloon angioplasty of the HV-IVC junction and
IVC/RA junction will be necessary.
